content:
## Task
Improve the post-route quality of `cmp32` (32-bit registered unsigned comparator: y = (a < b)) without changing its behavior.

## Specification (current RTL, also the equivalence reference)
```verilog
module cmp32 (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst_n,
    input wire valid_i,
    input wire [31:0] a_i,
    input wire [31:0] b_i,
    output reg valid_o,
    output reg [0:0] y_o
);

wire lt_0 = (a_i[31:0] < b_i[31:0]);
wire eq_0 = (a_i[31:0] == b_i[31:0]);

wire cmp_0 = lt_0;

always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (!rst_n) begin
        valid_o <= 1'b0;
        y_o <= 1'd0;
    end else begin
        valid_o <= valid_i;
        if (valid_i)
            y_o <= cmp_0;
    end
end
endmodule
```
Your design must be cycle-for-cycle equivalent to this module from reset: same ports, synchronous active-low reset, `valid_o` follows `valid_i` one cycle later, and `y_o` updates only on valid cycles and holds otherwise.

## Flow and objective
Yosys/ABC synthesis to the Nangate45 library, then OpenROAD placement, clock tree synthesis and routing with a 10 ns clock and a fixed floorplan. Score = 10 * WNS_ns - 0.001 * area_um2, where WNS is the worst setup slack after routing and area is total standard-cell area. Higher is better.

This RTL measured: area 268.926 um^2, WNS 7.62112 ns, score 75.942274.
estimate_ppa on this RTL returns area 177.156 um^2, WNS 7.69083 ns, estimated score 76.731144 (estimates omit tap cells, buffering and wiring, so compare estimates with estimates).

## Rules
- One module of synthesizable Verilog-2005 (no helper modules or instances; the equivalence checker compares flat modules). The module name and ports must not change.
- No initial blocks, system tasks, compiler directives or technology cells.
- place_and_route budget: 4 submissions. Every submission counts, including failed ones.
- At most 30 tool calls in total.

Tools available: simulate, prove_equivalence, estimate_ppa, place_and_route, finish. Your score is the best verified place_and_route score. Call finish when you are done.

content.text: I'll start by testing two restructured comparator architectures against the baseline estimate.
Both restructurings give essentially the same result — suggesting a large fixed component in the path. Let me probe the floor.
Useful data: the "floor" (1 gate) is WNS 7.911, so logic depth costs ~0.2 ns. Since 0.1 ns ≈ 1.0 reward but 100 um² ≈ 0.1 reward, **delay dominates**. Let me hunt for the shallowest structure.
Best so far is the plain 32-mux ripple (7.715 ns, 114 um²). Let me verify it and simultaneously test an output-stage variant.

Post-route tracks the estimate with a ~-0.075 ns shift and +92 um². Let me calibrate the achievable delay floor and test a cheaper prefix formulation (borrow chain: p = ~a|b instead of XNOR).
Calibration: a shallow 64-input function tops out at 7.785 ns, so we're within 0.07 ns of the ceiling. Let me probe two more ripple forms.
Everything converges near 7.71 — ABC is already mapping near the depth limit. Two last structural ideas:
The 4-bit-group + SOP top level jumped to 7.730. Let me refine that direction.
Best candidate: 4-bit mux-ripple groups + flat 8-term SOP (est 7.730 / 149 um²). Verifying it.

content.text: I've used my call budget nearly up. The best verified result stands at score 76.223 (submission 2), and no remaining candidate has a better estimate than the one already placed and routed.

input.summary: I first calibrated the design space: a trivial 1-gate design reaches WNS 7.911 ns while a shallow 64-input function reaches 7.785 ns, showing that (a) the scoring is dominated by delay (0.1 ns ≈ 1.0 reward vs 100 um² ≈ 0.1 reward) and (b) only ~0.2 ns of logic delay is in play, i.e. ABC was already mapping the comparator near its depth limit. I then swept ~15 structural formulations (Kogge-Stone-style g/p prefix trees at radix 2 and 4, dual-rail mutually-exclusive lt/gt trees with single-gate AOI21/OAI21 merges, borrow-chain ripples, adder-carry form, 8/16-bit split with equality combine, suffix-AND sum-of-products, and mux-ripple chains), all of which landed in a narrow 7.65–7.73 ns band, plus an output-stage rewrite (d = (valid&rst)&lt | (~valid&rst)&y) that removes the synchronous-reset gate from the critical path. The best structure was 8 groups of 4 bits, each group a small compare, combined by a flat 8-term sum-of-products carry expression: estimate 7.730 ns / 149 um², post-route WNS 7.64634 ns, area 239.9 um², score 76.223 (baseline 75.942, +0.281). Both simulation and formal equivalence were proven before each of the two place-and-route submissions.
